evidence: All five dimensions are mode = "batched" (judge.toml line 3 each). Gates render/constraints use aggregation = "all_pass" (judge.toml:15) and are exempt. The three scored dimensions (weighted_mean; 57 '^name' lines across the three scored judge.toml files; polish 5 binary, visual 5 likert, remainder functional binary) each carry explicit independence-and-continue wording: functional/prompt.md:13 'Once it succeeds, score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures and keep successful observations. A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row. Shared protocols reduce setup; they are not conjunctive bundles. When a setup step fails, set up the same thing again on a new job of your own...'; functional/prompt.md:7 (shared 'Grading only' block in all three) 'give that criterion its lowest score ... state what you observed, and move on'; functional/prompt.md:23 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row'; polish/prompt.md:12 'Otherwise judge each criterion independently and continue after failures.'; visual/prompt.md:12 'Otherwise grade every criterion independently with its five anchors and continue after failures.'; all three line 16/18/53 'return binary0 [raw Likert1] for the unobserved outcome ... Preserve every completed independent observation.' The only all-or-nothing rule is the global browser gate (functional:13, polish:12, visual:12), which mirrors the template's 'If the gate fails, assign 0 to every criterion in this dimension' and is permitted. Grep for stop/abort/halt/first fail/rest of/conjunct across scored prompts, scored judge.toml and app_context.md found no stop-at-first-failure instruction. Cross-row phrases in functional/judge.toml (e.g. :65 'Arrival of several cards together belongs to hro_bulk_move', :110 'Overfill by a multi-card move belongs to hro_bulk_places and by undo to hro_undo_full', :236 'graded only in hro_undo_conflict') are attribution/dedup statements, not conditional zeroing; no criterion says it fails because another failed. Per-criterion 'Fails if any condition stated above does not hold' is intra-criterion conjunction, which the skill (known false positives, 'One criterion covering a whole flow') allows. Adversarial probes: (a) broken app that fails early protocol S job intake but has a working board otherwise: job opening is also the gate, so all-zero is the intended gate rule; if only a sub-rule of S fails (e.g. blank title accepted) the prompt tells the judge to score hro_job_open 0 and keep going, so later rows are not zeroed. (b) conforming alternative lacking a multi-select UI shape the judge expects: functional:23 tells the judge to record 'not offered' and replay the observed request, and :13 re-setup clause keeps dependent rows observable, so one missing control cannot zero the rest. Template comparison: the task's wording is at least as strong as template polish/visual 'Independent scoring' sections and template functional 'Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure'. Deterministic counterpart check-batched-independence-wording.py was not executed here (private checker not available to this reviewer); manual application of its documented behaviour passes. Not measured: whether the configured claude-code judge actually honors this wording at runtime — raw-evidence-index.json states full configured grading is absent; this row grades prompt wording, which is source-verifiable, so that gap does not block this row but is owned by the runtime rows.
